objectives: Trace cosmology from pre-modern thought through Hubble.
Contrast Big Bang vs Steady State.
State the cosmological principle + observational pillars.

slides.title: From ancient cosmologies to the relativistic universe (1917-1929)
slides.body:
**Pre-modern cosmology**: nearly every culture built a model — Babylonian celestial spheres, Aristotelian geocentric crystalline spheres, Ptolemy's epicycles (Almagest, ~150 CE) — all static + Earth-centered. **Copernicus 1543** (heliocentric) + **Kepler 1609-1619** (elliptical orbits) + **Galileo 1610** (telescopic discoveries) + **Newton 1687** (Principia, universal gravitation) gave a heliocentric solar system, but the universe at large was still implicitly static + eternal.

**Olbers' paradox** (Halley 1721; restated Olbers 1823): why is the night sky dark? An infinite, eternal, static universe of stars would have every line of sight ending on a stellar surface — the sky would be as bright as the Sun's. The darkness is a clue.

**Einstein 1917 — first relativistic cosmology**: applied his 1915 General Relativity to the cosmos. Assuming a static + closed universe, he added the **cosmological constant Λ** to balance gravitational collapse — yielding the **Einstein static universe** (S³ spatial geometry, finite, unbounded). He later called Λ his 'biggest blunder' when expansion was discovered; ironically Λ returned in 1998 as dark energy.

**Friedmann 1922-1924** (St Petersburg meteorologist + mathematician): solved Einstein's equations under homogeneity + isotropy without imposing staticity. Found a family of **expanding (or contracting) solutions** parameterized by spatial curvature (k = +1, 0, −1) — the Friedmann equations. Einstein initially dismissed them; later acknowledged Friedmann correct. Died of typhoid at 37 (1925), before vindication.

**Lemaître 1927** (Belgian priest + cosmologist): independently rediscovered the expanding solutions, derived v = H·d theoretically, + proposed the universe began from a **'primeval atom'** or 'cosmic egg' — the first explicit Big Bang concept. Published in obscure Annales de la Société Scientifique de Bruxelles; ignored until Eddington translated it (1931). Lemaître first interpreted galaxy redshifts as expansion. **Hubble 1929** (Mt Wilson, with Humason): measured Cepheid distances + redshifts of 24 galaxies, plotted v vs d, found linear relation v = H_0 · d. Confirmed expansion empirically. Hubble himself remained agnostic about cosmological interpretation — Lemaître + Einstein supplied the theory.

**Hubble's number was wrong** (H_0 ≈ 500 km/s/Mpc) due to Cepheid calibration errors — yielding age ~2 Gyr, younger than Earth! Took until Baade 1952 (Population I/II Cepheids) + Sandage 1958 to revise H_0 down + age up to ~13 Gyr.

slides.title: Big Bang vs Steady State + the CMB clincher
slides.body:
**1940s-50s — two rival cosmologies**:

**Big Bang** (term coined dismissively by **Fred Hoyle** on BBC radio 1949 — the name stuck): universe began hot + dense, has expanded + cooled, evolves over cosmic time. **George Gamow** (Russian-American physicist, student of Friedmann) + students **Ralph Alpher** + **Robert Herman** (1948) developed **Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN)**: in the first few minutes, hot dense plasma fused H + He from protons + neutrons. Their famous α-β-γ paper (Alpher-Bethe-Gamow 1948 — Bethe added jokingly) predicted primordial He ~25% (matched observations). Alpher + Herman 1948 then predicted a **relic radiation** at ~5 K — the cosmic microwave background — left over from when matter + photons decoupled. The prediction was largely forgotten.

**Steady State** (Bondi + Gold 1948; Hoyle 1948): universe is eternal + unchanging on large scales, despite expansion, via **continuous creation** of matter (~1 atom/m³/Gyr) to maintain constant density. Aesthetically pleasing (no beginning, true 'perfect cosmological principle'). Hoyle was Steady State's defender + a brilliant nucleosynthesis pioneer (B²FH paper 1957 — Burbidge + Burbidge + Fowler + Hoyle — explained stellar nucleosynthesis of heavy elements).

**Penzias + Wilson 1964** (Bell Labs, Holmdel NJ): debugging a horn antenna for satellite communications, found unexplained 3 K excess noise from all directions. Independently, **Dicke + Peebles + Wilkinson + Roll** at Princeton were building a radiometer to search for exactly the Gamow-Alpher-Herman prediction. Penzias heard of the Princeton effort + the two papers appeared back-to-back in ApJ 1965 — Penzias + Wilson reporting the measurement, Dicke et al. interpreting it as the relic Big Bang radiation. Penzias + Wilson shared the **1978 Nobel** (with Kapitsa for low-T physics). Steady State was effectively falsified: a relic radiation field from a hot dense past has no place in an eternal universe.

**Subsequent confirmations**:
- **COBE** (Mather + Smoot, 1989-1992 → 2006 Nobel): blackbody at 2.725 K to extraordinary precision; first detection of anisotropies (ΔT/T ~ 10⁻⁵).
- **WMAP** (2001-2010): precision angular power spectrum → ΛCDM parameters.
- **Planck** (2009-2013, results 2013/2015/2018): definitive measurement; Ω_m = 0.315, Ω_Λ = 0.685, H_0 = 67.4 ± 0.5 km/s/Mpc, age = 13.797 ± 0.023 Gyr.
- **BBN element abundances**: H ~75%, He ~25%, D + ³He + ⁷Li at trace — consistent with Ω_b ≈ 0.05.
- **Galaxy redshift surveys** (Sloan SDSS, 2dF, DES, DESI): large-scale structure consistent with growth from inflationary seeds.

slides.title: The cosmological principle + observational pillars
slides.body:
**Cosmological principle** (CP): on sufficiently large scales (≳ 100 Mpc), the universe is **homogeneous** (no preferred location) + **isotropic** (no preferred direction). A simplifying assumption + an empirical claim — increasingly tested.

**Perfect cosmological principle** (Bondi + Gold + Hoyle 1948 Steady State): adds homogeneity in **time** — universe looks the same at every epoch. Falsified by CMB + galaxy evolution (high-z galaxies are systematically different from low-z).

**Why CP is reasonable**:
- **Isotropy**: CMB is isotropic to ΔT/T ~ 10⁻⁵ after removing dipole (our motion at 369 km/s w.r.t. CMB rest frame); galaxy counts in large redshift surveys are isotropic.
- **Homogeneity**: galaxy two-point correlation function ξ(r) → 0 at large r (~100 Mpc end of homogeneity). Confirmed by SDSS, 2dF, DESI.
- **Copernican principle**: we are not in a privileged position; combined with isotropy → homogeneity (a CP if true for all observers).

**Caveats + frontiers**:
- **Inhomogeneity at small scales**: galaxies + clusters + voids + filaments at <100 Mpc.
- **Possible anomalies**: cold spot in CMB; quadrupole-octopole alignment ('axis of evil'); large-scale dipoles in galaxy/quasar distributions (Singal 2011; Secrest 2021) — slightly tense with CP; mostly attributed to statistical fluctuations or instrumental.
- **'Just an assumption'**: technically the CP is built into FLRW; alternative inhomogeneous (Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi) models exist + are tested.

**Six observational pillars of modern cosmology** (Big Bang + ΛCDM):
1. **Hubble flow** (1929 → today): expanding universe; v ≈ H_0·d at low z; cosmological redshift at all z. Confirmed by Type Ia SNe (standard candles) + galaxy surveys.
2. **CMB blackbody + anisotropies** (Penzias-Wilson 1965, COBE 1992, WMAP, Planck): relic from recombination (z ≈ 1100), TCMB = 2.725 K, anisotropies encode early-universe physics.
3. **BBN light-element abundances** (~75% H, ~25% He, trace D + ³He + ⁷Li): match prediction from t ~ 1 s to ~20 min hot dense epoch.
4. **Large-scale structure** (LSS): galaxies trace filaments + voids; matter power spectrum P(k); growth function D(z) consistent with ΛCDM.
5. **Type Ia supernovae** (Perlmutter + Schmidt + Riess 1998 → 2011 Nobel): high-z SNe Ia dimmer than expected → accelerating expansion → dark energy.
6. **Baryon acoustic oscillations** (BAO; SDSS 2005, BOSS, eBOSS, DESI 2024): sound-horizon standard ruler at 150 Mpc imprinted on galaxy clustering — independent geometric probe.

**Standard ΛCDM parameters (Planck 2018)**:
- H_0 = 67.4 km/s/Mpc (CMB)
- Ω_m = 0.315, Ω_Λ = 0.685, Ω_b = 0.049, Ω_k ≈ 0 (flat)
- σ_8 = 0.811, n_s = 0.965
- Age = 13.797 ± 0.023 Gyr
- Composition: ~69% dark energy, ~26% dark matter, ~5% baryons

The Big Bang + ΛCDM model is the **standard cosmology** — six numbers fit thousands of independent observations. Tensions (Hubble + S8) hint at possible new physics, treated in the modern-frontier lesson.

question.question: Estimate the Hubble time + critique it
question.goal: Given H_0 = 70 km/s/Mpc, compute the Hubble time t_H = 1/H_0 in Gyr + discuss its relation to the true age.

steps.prompt: Convert H_0 = 70 km/s/Mpc to SI units (1/s).
steps.reveal: H_0 = 70 (km/s)/Mpc × (1 Mpc / 3.086×10^19 km) = 2.27×10⁻¹⁸ s⁻¹. The Hubble constant has units of inverse time.

steps.prompt: Compare with the actual age from Planck (13.797 Gyr).

acceptedAnswers: Hubble time ≈ true age within a few percent — accident of ΛCDM

hints: Matter universe: age = (2/3)·t_H; Λ-only: t_H exactly.
steps.reveal: Pure matter universe → age = (2/3)·t_H ≈ 9.3 Gyr (too young). Λ-only de Sitter → age = t_H. ΛCDM with Ω_m = 0.31, Ω_Λ = 0.69 → age ≈ 0.96·t_H = 13.5 Gyr ≈ 13.797 (Planck). The 'Hubble time' is a remarkably good zeroth-order estimate — partly an accident of current matter+Λ balance.

steps.prompt: Why did Hubble's original H_0 ≈ 500 km/s/Mpc cause a crisis?

acceptedAnswers: t_H ≈ 2 Gyr, younger than Earth's age (~4.5 Gyr)

steps.reveal: t_H = 1/(500 km/s/Mpc) ≈ 2 Gyr — younger than radiometric Earth age (~4.5 Gyr, Patterson 1956). Glaring inconsistency. Baade 1952 separated Population I/II Cepheids → H_0 dropped ~factor 2; Sandage 1958 further refined to ~75. Modern values: Planck 67.4, SH0ES 73.0 — the Hubble tension.

question.question: Why did the Penzias-Wilson 1964 discovery effectively kill the Steady State theory?
options: The CMB is a 2.725 K relic blackbody filling all of space, predicted by Gamow + Alpher + Herman 1948 as the redshifted remnant of a hot dense early universe at ~3000 K (recombination, z ≈ 1100). Steady State (Bondi + Gold + Hoyle 1948) had no mechanism for such a perfectly thermalized isotropic radiation — its continuous-creation model required a static eternal cosmos. The CMB's perfection (best blackbody ever measured), isotropy, + redshift-consistent temperature were exactly what Big Bang predicted + Steady State could not accommodate. Penzias + Wilson won the 1978 Nobel; the Dicke-Peebles-Wilkinson interpretation appeared back-to-back in ApJ 1965. Combined with BBN light-element abundances (75% H, 25% He from t ~ 100 s hot dense phase), the Big Bang became the standard cosmology. Hoyle famously coined 'Big Bang' as a derisive term in 1949 — yet his term + his rival's victory both stuck.
question.explanation: CMB at 2.725 K is the predicted relic radiation from a hot dense early universe (Gamow + Alpher + Herman 1948); Steady State has no mechanism for such a thermalized isotropic field. Penzias + Wilson 1964 detection + Dicke-Peebles interpretation falsified Steady State; Big Bang + ΛCDM became standard cosmology. 1978 Nobel.

hints: What does the CMB imply about cosmic history?
Why can't Steady State produce it?
slides.workedSolution: CMB = relic blackbody from t ~ 380kyr, redshifted from ~3000K to 2.725K, predicted by Gamow-Alpher-Herman 1948. Steady State requires eternal static cosmos — no hot dense early phase, no mechanism for such a thermalized isotropic radiation. Penzias-Wilson 1964 + Dicke-Peebles 1965 → Big Bang wins. Combined with BBN, CMB is among the cleanest cosmological confirmations.

question.question: A new redshift survey reports a 1-Gpc dipole in galaxy counts at 5σ — significantly larger than the CMB dipole expectation from our motion.
question.prompt: How would this affect the cosmological principle? What systematic effects must be ruled out? What other observations (CMB, BAO, SNe Ia) would corroborate or refute the result? Mention Secrest et al. 2021 + the radio-galaxy + quasar dipole anomalies + how they relate to the 'cosmic dipole tension'.

question.question: Write Hubble's law in algebraic form (recessional velocity vs distance).
question.hint: Linear relation; constant of proportionality is the Hubble parameter at present.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, summarize the historical arc from Einstein's static 1917 universe to the modern ΛCDM concordance.
question.rubric: Mentions: Einstein 1917 added cosmological constant Λ to enforce a static universe under GR. Friedmann 1922-24 + Lemaître 1927 derived expanding solutions; Lemaître proposed the primeval atom (proto-Big Bang). Hubble 1929 empirically discovered v = H_0·d. Gamow + Alpher + Herman 1948 predicted BBN + CMB. Hoyle + Bondi + Gold 1948 Steady State rivalry; Hoyle coined 'Big Bang' derisively. Penzias + Wilson 1964 → CMB detection → Dicke-Peebles 1965 interpretation → Steady State falsified; 1978 Nobel. COBE 1992 (anisotropies, blackbody, 2006 Nobel); WMAP 2003; Planck 2013/2018. Perlmutter-Schmidt-Riess 1998 discover accelerating expansion → 2011 Nobel. ΛCDM = matter (5% baryon + 26% DM) + 69% Λ + flat geometry — six numbers fit thousands of observations. Modern tensions (H_0, S_8) hint at possible new physics.
